terra.problem: The joke treats the passage’s personification of the land as the punchline. Scripture’s wording and imagery should not be the joke.
The passage does not say that nobody in the desert is hanging their head.
Sorrow flees in verse 10, but the text does not say it is scared or that nothing else is afraid.
The verse describes the blooming and says they will see the LORD’s glory, but it does not say the blooming points past itself.
The quoted message has five words, not three.
The explanation directly assigns the message to the individual baker, though the text addresses those with anxious hearts without identifying the baker as one of them.
“Nobody gets left out” makes a universal claim the verse does not make.
The verse says the lame will leap, but it does not say they will not walk or shuffle.
The verse does not say nobody is sitting down.
Leaping like a deer does not establish that they are moving fast.
The claim that these trees appear elsewhere in Isaiah needs a reference to that passage.
“This road keeps them off” adds a mechanism the text does not give. It says fools will not stray onto it.
“No wrong turns on this one” claims more than the verse says. It says fools will not stray onto the Way, not that no one on it makes a wrong turn.
The text says they enter singing, but it does not say they do not tiptoe.
Calling Zion the city of God draws on a fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation assumes the redeemed have been through hard things. The text does not say that about them.
Calling Zion the city of God draws on a fact outside this passage and needs a reference.
